name: Intramedullary Non-Dysraphic Spinal Cord Lipoma

criteria.description: MRI evidence of intramedullary lipomatous lesion without associated spinal dysraphism
Presence of progressive neurological deficits consistent with spinal cord compression
Histopathological confirmation of mature adipose tissue within spinal cord parenchyma
No evidence of spinal dysraphism or associated cutaneous stigmata

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: MRI evidence of intramedullary lipoma without dysraphism plus compatible neurological signs
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Histopathology is confirmatory but not always required if imaging and clinical presentation are typical.

searchTerms: gradual stiffness and weakness in legs

pathognomonic.symptomName: Sensory level deficit corresponding to lesion site
searchTerms: loss of sensation at injury level
sensory loss at affected spinal level

common.symptomName: Localized back pain at lesion level

searchTerms: difficulty walking due to leg weakness
loss of muscle bulk in affected area

rare.symptomName: Spinal cord ischemia secondary to compression
searchTerms: spinal cord blood flow loss from pressure
spinal cord damage due to compression

rare.symptomName: Cutaneous stigmata (rarely present despite non-dysraphic classification)
searchTerms: skin marks or birthmarks near spine

laboratory: Routine labs typically normal; no specific biomarkers identified
imaging: MRI showing well-demarcated intramedullary lesion with fat signal characteristics (hyperintense on T1-weighted images, suppressed on fat-saturation sequences)
Absence of spinal dysraphism or tethered cord on imaging
genetic: No known genetic mutations associated; sporadic occurrence
other: Histopathology reveals mature adipocytes within spinal cord parenchyma without atypia

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of spinal dysraphism or cutaneous stigmata
Different surgical approach due to dysraphism

redFlags: Acute onset of bladder or bowel incontinence
Signs of spinal cord ischemia or infarction
references: Takahashi M, et al. Intramedullary spinal cord lipomas without spinal dysraphism: clinical features and surgical outcomes. Neurosurgery. 2018;82(3):345-352.
Orphanet: Intramedullary non-dysraphic spinal cord lipoma (ORPHA:645359)
Klekamp J. Intramedullary spinal cord tumors: diagnosis and treatment. Neurosurg Rev. 2017;40(4):569-579.
